mainEntity.name: Can my windscreen be replaced at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. That's how we do most jobs. We come to your home, your workplace or wherever the car has stopped, and fit the glass on site. We need room to open both front doors and walk the length of the windscreen, and somewhere reasonably sheltered if it's raining hard, because urethane adhesive doesn't cure properly in the wet.

mainEntity.name: How long does a windscreen replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The fitting itself is usually the shortest part of the visit. What extends it is the adhesive cure time before the car is safe to drive, and recalibration if your vehicle has a camera behind the glass. We'll give you the full picture when you book, including exactly how long before the car is safe to drive, so you can plan the day around it.

mainEntity.name: Is it illegal to drive with a cracked windscreen in NSW?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be. NSW road rules require a windscreen that doesn't obstruct the driver's view, and damage in the driver's line of sight is the clearest problem. It can attract a defect notice and it's commonly picked up at inspection. Cracks near the edge of the glass are also treated seriously because they compromise the windscreen's structural role. If you're unsure whether yours crosses the line, send us a photo.

Most comprehensive policies in NSW do, often with a separate glass excess that's lower than the standard excess, and some include one glass claim a year at no excess. Whether it's worth claiming depends on how your excess compares to the cost of the job. Check your policy or ask your insurer: cover varies, and this is general information rather than advice on your situation.

mainEntity.name: Do you repair chips, or only replace?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both, and we'll tell you honestly which one your damage needs. A chip smaller than a 20-cent coin, away from the edge and out of the driver's line of sight, can usually be repaired. Repairs are quicker and cost less, and they keep the factory-bonded glass in the car. See windscreen chip repair for what can and can't be saved.

mainEntity.name: Do you do trucks as well as cars?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We fit heavy vehicle glass at depots, yards and roadside across the Sydney metro area, and we work with fleet operators where downtime is the real cost rather than the glass. See truck windscreen replacement.

We service the Sydney metro area only. We're based at Chipping Norton, so the south-west and west are our closest runs, but we work from the western suburbs through to the eastern suburbs and up to the northern beaches. Tell us where the vehicle is and we'll tell you straight away whether we can get to it.
